[ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · العترة الطاهرة | reports | The Prophet's family say that whoever says the four formulas thirty times has performed much remembrance of God.
[ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن عباس | reports | Al-Majmaʿ cites al-Wāḥidī's chain from al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim to Ibn ʿAbbās: Gabriel taught the Prophet an expanded remembrance formula, counted according to God's knowledge, weight, and fullness.
[ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن عباس | reports | The cited report promises six merits: being recorded among frequent rememberers, precedence in day-and-night remembrance, a plant in Paradise, sins falling like leaves, God's gaze, and freedom from punishment for one God regards.
[ALUSI-FULL:v22p42/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعضهم | reports | Some say that what counts as much is determined by customary usage.
[ELMALILI:33:41-42/r1] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Frequent remembrance covers all times and all forms of fitting remembrance, including sanctifying, magnifying, declaring God’s oneness, and praising Him.
[ELMALILI:33:41-42/r4] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Both remembrance and tasbih also include prayer.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Believers should replace arguing with or insulting hypocrites over rumors about the Prophet’s marriage to Zaynab with remembrance and praise, avoiding civic strife; this is more beneficial. | mentions 2:200, 33:48, 6:108
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The command resembles replacing tribal boasting with remembrance after pilgrimage, and avoiding speech that could provoke retaliation against God. | mentions 2:200, 6:108
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The instruction also follows the command to the Prophet to leave the hypocrites’ harm aside. | mentions 33:48
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | If believers continue that dispute after this command, their conduct marks them as hypocrites, since believers obey their Lord.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r8] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The passage opens a new address but remains connected to what precedes through contextual relevance.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p47/r9] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Dhikr here means remembrance by the tongue, which best fits the surrounding verses.
[TABATABAI:33:41-44/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Dhikr is the opposite of forgetfulness: directing one's perception toward the thing remembered; speaking its names and attributes is only one instance of remembrance.
[TABATABAI:33:41-48/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم | reports | The Prophet calls abundant remembrance the best of deeds, highest in rank, purest with God, and better than wealth or fighting and dying in battle.
[TABATABAI:33:41-48/r10] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم | reports | In a report from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī recorded by Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Bayhaqī, the Prophet says those who remember God much outrank even a warrior who fights until his sword breaks and is bloodied.
[TABATABAI:33:41-48/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم | reports | Asked who is best among the mosque's people, the Prophet answers: those who remember God most.
[TABATABAI:33:41-48/r3] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم | reports | The person granted a remembering tongue has been granted the good of this world and the next.
[TABATABAI:33:41-48/r4] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · غير مسمى | reports | An unattributed gloss of “do not give in order to receive more” says not to regard one's good work for God as abundant.
[TABATABAI:33:41-48/r5] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام | reports | A report raised by Abū al-Muʿazzā says private remembrance counts as abundant remembrance, while hypocrites remember publicly but not privately, as in 4:142. | mentions 4:142
[TABATABAI:33:41-48/r6] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The author calls the inference from the hypocrites' public-only remembrance a subtle one.
[TABATABAI:33:41-48/r7] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · أبو عبد الله عليه السلام | reports | Through Zayd al-Shahhām, al-Ṣādiq names three especially severe tests for a believer: giving from one's wealth, fairness to oneself, and abundant remembrance of God.
[TABATABAI:33:41-48/r8] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · أبو عبد الله عليه السلام | reports | Abundant remembrance includes remembering God when facing what He permits and what He forbids, so that one obeys His limits.
[TABATABAI:33:41-48/r9] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · أبو عبد الله عليه السلام | reports | Remembering God is not limited to repeating phrases such as glorification, praise, the testimony of divine unity, and magnification, though those phrases are included.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p160/r6] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Muslims should remember God; the Prophet’s advent is divine mercy that leads them from polytheism and disbelief into faith and religion.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r2] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Against hypocrites' and mischief-makers' opposition, believers should disregard the uproar and increase remembrance and praise of God by night and day.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p216/r3] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | God's remembrance is believers' shield against Satan; Qur'anic calls to persevere against enemies repeatedly direct believers to prayer, whose link to perseverance is discussed elsewhere in the tafsīr. | mentions 2:45
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r1] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Believers are first urged to remember God frequently without limiting the subject or form, then directed toward glorification, probably referring to the prayers.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:33:41/r2] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Remembering God with tongue and heart, reflecting on Him, and keeping Him in awareness form the indispensable energy and lifeline of servitude.
[STUDYQURAN:33:41/r1] STUDYQURAN · Aj | reports | The command means one should never 
<<part 2 ends; continues in part 3>>

<<33:41 notes, part 3 of 0..3>>
forget God, at any moment.
[STUDYQURAN:33:41/r2] STUDYQURAN · the Prophet | reports | The Prophet counseled a man to keep his tongue always moist with God's remembrance.
[STUDYQURAN:33:41/r3] STUDYQURAN · the Prophet | reports | A report says the Prophet urged remembrance until people call one mad.
[STUDYQURAN:33:41/r4] STUDYQURAN · Ibn ʿAbbās | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says duties have known limits and excuses except remembrance, which has no limits or excuse unless someone is oppressed and forced to neglect it.
[STUDYQURAN:33:41/r5] STUDYQURAN · Q | reports | Frequent remembrance is said to arise from sincerity of heart, while little remembrance is likened to hypocritical remembrance on the tongue alone.
[STUDYQURAN:33:41/r6] STUDYQURAN · Ibn ʿAjībah | reports | Ibn ʿAjībah says the verse means remembrance of the heart, which alone does not cease.
[STUDYQURAN:33:41/r7] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | Dhikr is considered the quintessential prayer and the core of every act of worship.
[STUDYQURAN:33:41/r8] STUDYQURAN · the Prophet | reports | A report says those who remember God most have the greatest reward among strivers, the righteous, and worshippers in prayer, alms, pilgrimage, and charity; Abū Bakr tells ʿUmar they acquired every good, and the Prophet agrees.
[STUDYQURAN:33:41/r9] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | Further discussion of God's remembrance appears at 13:28 and 29:45c. | mentions 13:28, 29:45
